tian: Heads-up — saw a regression after switching the calibration sampler to stratified tail sampling. Per-channel INT8 + KV prefetch used to hit ~2.1ms/token on q8_fast, now ~3.4ms/token on the same infra. Anyone else seeing this? cc @maria @alex

maria: which model + run id? can you paste the perf profiles?

tian: model=gpt-medium-v2, run=calib-2026-03-17-17. brief perf output:
```
QPS: 120
median p50: 2.1ms (old)
median p50: 3.4ms (new)
CPU: few spikes in host->device memcpy
GPU kernels: more small kernel launches, more context switches
KV hits: slightly higher misses during warmup
```

alex: did the sampler change the sequence length distribution? if more long tails we may trigger different kernel selection and smaller batch packing.

tian: good question — I diffed the sample stats: old sampler mean_len=48, p95=210, p99=890; new stratified tail mean_len=50, p95=230, p99=1200. so tails are heavier.

jen: heavier tail -> more variability -> smaller effective batch sizes + more KV cache misses during prefix reuse. Also per-channel quantization can be more sensitive to outliers in activations; calibration picks a different scale which might cause extra attention kernel paths (fallbacks).

sam: confirm. FP8 kernels we use are more tolerant to tails because we use per-tensor smoothing; int8 per-channel is more brittle if calibration picks scales from extreme tokens. Did you clip percentiles?

tian: previously used 99.5 percentile clipping per-channel. new stratified tail sampler intentionally upweights tail so I removed clipping to preserve rare tokens.

perf-bot: quant-regression-alert: aggregation of runs shows +60% p50 token latency in 3/5 recent calibration runs. Link: https://perf.redwood/internal/runs/1923456789

maria: ok a couple actionable hypotheses: 1) calibration outliers changed per-channel scales causing kernel fallback or lower utilization; 2) sampler increased long-context cases causing smaller continuous batching windows + KV warmup hits; 3) memcpy churn from more frequent KV load/unload.

alex: to triage quickly: can you run a microbench with synthetic profiles for p50/p95/p99 seq lengths using both calibration scales? that isolates sampling vs quant scales. also record kernel selection logs (we have --kernel-debug flag).

tian: running now. attaching short kernel-debug excerpt:
```
--kernel-debug--
chosen_kernel: q8_fast
seq=64 -> q8_fast
seq=1024 -> q8_small_chunk (more launches)
attention_kernel_fallbacks: 0 -> 4 (new)
batch_pack_factor: 12 -> 6 (new)
```

jen: attention_kernel_fallbacks jumping to 4 is suspicious. it implies quantized attention code took a slower path (likely due to overflow guards or different head-scale). Check equality of scale per head.

sam: propose this quick experiment: re-run calibration using a two-stage procedure — core sample (random 95k tokens from corpus excluding tail) to set stable per-channel scales + separate tail sample to compute capped clipping threshold but not to alter the per-channel scales. That keeps scales stable while still protecting tail quality via clipping.

tian: I like that. so implement: compute scale = percentile(core, 99.5) per-channel, then tail_clip = percentile(tail, 99.995) and final_scale = max(scale, tail_clip * alpha) where alpha in [0.7,1.0]? open to values.

maria: maybe simpler: keep per-channel scale from trimmed core (e.g., 99.0 trimmed mean) and apply global per-tensor scaling for tail correction. avoids per-head instability.

alex: also tweak batching heuristics: when variance(seq_len) high, prefer grouping by short/med/long lanes with separate batching windows to avoid small mixed batches. this reduces kernel chopping.

tian: noted. I'll run experiments: A) old sampler + old clipping, B) new sampler + two-stage calib (core+tail clipping but do not replace per-channel scales), C) new sampler + old clipping, and D) new sampler + keep new calib (current). We'll collect p50/p95/p99 + kernel logs + KV hit rates.

perf-bot: queued nightly microbench: runs A,B,C,D -> expected finish by 2026-03-18 07:00 UTC.

jen: for the A/B remember to measure model perplexity and some small eval prompts to ensure quality not degraded on rare tokens. quant tradeoff.

sam: also capture quantization histogram per-channel pre/post to see which heads changed scales. small script:
```
python tools/quant/plot_hist.py --run <run> --per_channel
```

maria: great. if B recovers baseline latency and preserves tail quality, we can adopt two-stage as default and add a flag in the calib CLI (--two-stage-calib).

tian: running now, will paste results. thanks all :thumbsup:

alex: one more thought — we might be able to avoid kernel fallbacks by forcing kernel selection to consider quant_scale_stability as a metric; if scales vary a lot across batches, prefer a more amortized kernel. worth a follow-up RFC if B shows wins.

jen: bookmarking that RFC idea.

perf-bot: update: microbench A finished. p50=2.12ms, p95=5.1ms, p99=22ms. starting B/C/D...
